title: 4.2 Please turn off the TV
unit_title: Life at home, every day and yesterday
unit_outcome: Say where people and things are at home, talk about the lights and machines, ask what there is, describe someone's morning in order, say what you did yesterday and on which day, ask and tell the time, say how often you do things and give dates.
goal: Ask someone to turn a lamp, a TV or a computer on or off, and say whether it is on or off (Please turn off the TV. / The lamp is on.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 4.2 Furniture and Home Objects: A1 names a lamp, a computer and other home objects; A1+ 4.2 switches them. The new items are turn on and turn off in a request with please (Please turn off the TV.), 2.12's command form, and on and off after be for the state (The lamp is on. / Is the computer on? No, it's off.). Each thing is photographed twice from the same camera, on and off, with its person's hand on the switch, the remote or the key: Ana's floor lamp, Luis's TV and Diego's laptop. A request is shown with the thing still in the state it asks to change, and request banks change only the thing, never on and off, so the picture never has to decide between them; on and off are set against each other only in sentences about the state, which the picture shows. Learn and Listen play a request and its result as two turns, and the picture switches on the second turn.
prerequisite: A1 4.2 lamp and computer; A1+ 1.8 Luis watches TV; A1+ 2.12 please + a command; A1+ 2.4 it's and isn't.
speaking_outcome: Link turn on (tur-NON) and turn off (tur-NOFF); keep the f of off clear. Do not require native-like speed.
